narrative.northStar: The Rhodonite Specimen, put to work
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Rhodonite Specimen, put to work"**

The tools are cut from the same stone as itrium.id. That site is The Rhodonite Specimen (`DESIGN.md` in the `website` repository): a graphite matrix with a pink vein, where gray is the body and pink marks what a visitor should find. Here the specimen leaves the display case and goes onto the workbench. The world is the same: Plus Jakarta Sans for everything, graphite and paper, pastel pink with its two deepenings, flat tonal surfaces, pills and soft corners, one drawn arrow. Only the job changes. itrium.id persuades; a tool gets out of the way. The index is The Device Map, one calm atlas plate: the visitor's device drawn as a single territory inside one border line in the text color, the two tools as places in it (a filled dot and an underlined bold name), and the only ways out drawn as dashed roads that cross the border to small outlined boxes, each labelled with what it carries. A legend in the margin column says the same as facts. Privacy is shown as geography, not claimed in a list. A tool page carries the map lightly: its title is a place mark (the place's dot beside the tool's name, no band), the work comes directly under it, and the tool's one road out hangs from the control that takes it, because the person using it is at a restaurant table with a phone in one hand and a group waiting.

Components are soft and sure-footed, and tactile without being playful. Every control has a round, generous target that a thumb finds the first time (2.75rem on touch screens) and an edge you can see (3:1 against the page and the card). They feel good to press but never perform. Density is calm but working: forms sit in a narrow column of 36 to 42rem, inset lists and notes nest one tonal step down inside cards, and the running total stays at the bottom of a phone's screen while the bill is made.

Light and dark are equal. Each follows the visitor's system, and neither is a courtesy version of the other: every new pairing is designed and checked in both. The system refuses what itrium.id refuses: generic SaaS ornament (gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers), drop shadows on anything but a floating list, pure black and white, decorative pink, and small labels above headings. It also refuses what only a tool can get wrong: a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen, and state shown by color alone.
keyCharacteristics: One stone with itrium.id: the same tokens, typeface, radii, button shapes and arrow.

The index is one map: the device as a territory with an irregular soft border, the tools as places in it, the roads out as dashed lines to outlined boxes, and a pink pill at each place, the two tools' equal starts. A tool page opens with a place mark, then the tool, with its one road out drawn under the control that takes it. The territory and the error page's band follow the theme: a step off the page, never the other theme's color.
Light and dark are equal. Both follow the system, unless System, Light or Dark is chosen in the footer.
Flat surfaces with tonal steps. The only shadow is under the open searchable list.
Every control has a 3:1 edge (`--control-border`), a target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens, and 16px text on touch screens so iOS doesn't zoom.
Pink marks the primary action, focus, what's selected, and the way onward, and nothing else.
Motion is CSS only and off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks something: the primary action, focus, what's selected, or the way onward. If you can't say what a pink element marks, it should be gray. Pink means one thing at a time, which is not the same as one element. In a tool, one pink button per view. On the index, a pink pill at each place, the two tools' equal starts ("Split a bill", "Chat with a number"): two pills, one meaning, the primary action. Rose-text action lines serve the tools elsewhere and a shared bill as their way onward, and nothing else is pink. The map's places, roads and border, a tool page's place mark and its road out are never pink.

rules.name: The Two Borders Rule
rules.body: `--border` is for lines nothing depends on, such as card edges and dividers. Anything a person has to find in order to use it gets `--control-border`.

rules.name: The Graphite Text Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite, never white. On light backgrounds pink text is rose text and pink lines are deep rose. Pastel pink is never text or a line there.

rules.name: The Every-Surface Rule
rules.body: Contrast is checked on every surface text sits on: page, card, inset list, note, running total, update notice, the index's territory and the page around it, in both themes. Text needs 4.5:1. Focus outlines, control edges and state lines need 3:1.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans does everything. Never add a second family, and never load a font from another domain.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A heading is the first thing in its block. No eyebrow, category label, small uppercase heading or back link sits above it. Nothing here is set in uppercase. A line that says more about a heading goes under it, as the index's name line and a place's line do.

rules.name: The One Map Rule
rules.body: The index is one map: the device as one territory, the tools as places in it, and every way out as a road crossing the border to an outlined box, labelled with what it carries. No cards, no bands, no rows of entries. A new tool is a new place; a new connection is a new road, drawn only when the site really makes one.

rules.name: The Kept Space Rule
rules.body: What the browser remembers arrives into a space already kept for it (the place's line holds three lines, 4.5rem, and the shared mark on phones 2.5rem), so nothing moves under a finger when it appears.

rules.name: The Slab Rule, for tools
rules.body: A tool page has no slab at either end: it opens with a place mark, a dot and the tool's name, and never closes with a panel. On a phone, the tool comes before the frame.

rules.name: The First Screen Rule
rules.body: On a phone, the first field of a tool is visible without scrolling. If a new element would push it down, it belongs lower on the page.

rules.name: The Answer In Reach Rule
rules.body: Wherever a tool is being filled in, its answer is one glance or one tap away: the running total below 1024 px, the split's own column above. Someone opening a shared result lands on it, not on the form that made it.

rules.name: The Only Floating Things Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons, chips, bands, the territory, the road boxes and the running total never get a drop shadow. A control responds by filling with the next tonal step, a place name by thickening its underline, and an arrow by moving 4 px on.

rules.name: The Inside The Line Rule
rules.body: Whatever stays on the device is drawn inside the territory, and whatever leaves it is drawn on a road outside it. Never put something that reaches a server inside the line, or draw a road the site doesn't take.

rules.name: The Hanging Road Rule
rules.body: A road out hangs from the one control that takes it, and only where the site really makes the connection. A friend's "Copy the link" copies the link they opened, which goes nowhere new, so no road is drawn under it.

rules.name: The Whole Edge Rule
rules.body: A note is marked by its whole edge, never by a thick bar down one side.

dos: Do take tokens, radii, button shapes, the arrow and type roles from itrium.id's DESIGN.md before inventing anything. A difference between the two sites needs a reason a tool has and a page doesn't.
Do keep a tool's first field on the first phone screen.
Do give every field, button and chip a `--control-border` edge and a touch target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens.

Do show every state in two ways: a check mark with the pink fill, words with the pink edge, and the reason a button can't be pressed yet, said under it when someone presses or reaches it (not at rest, and not read out again after every add).
Do design and check every new pairing in light and dark, on every surface it sits on.
Do use the drawn arrow wherever a link points onward.

Do keep motion in CSS, gated on `motion-safe` or `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`: page cross-fades, the 4 px arrow nudge, and the loading spinner. Nothing in a tool rises or reveals as it scrolls.

Do add to the index as the map: a tool as a place inside the territory with its pink start, a connection as a labelled road out to an outlined box, a fact as a line of the legend with its drawn swatch.
Do open a tool page with its place mark, and hang the tool's road out from the control that takes it, in the same words as its road on the index.
Do use Tailwind classes with the theme tokens and the shared classes in `src/lib/styles.ts`, never raw hex values in markup.
donts: Don't use pink as decoration, or give pink two meanings in one view: a tool has one pink button, and the index's two pills are both the primary action, one at each place.
Don't put a small uppercase heading, eyebrow, kicker or back link above a heading.
Don't type arrows or chevrons as characters.
Don't give cards, buttons, chips, bands or the running total a drop shadow.
Don't use `#000000` or pure white text on pink. Graphite is `#2b2b2b`.
Don't put pastel pink text or lines on a light background.
Don't use a native `<select>`, inline styles, `data:` URLs, or anything from another domain.
Don't add gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers, or a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen.
Don't set field text below 16px on touch screens.
Don't put cards, bands, a hero or rows of entries on the index, or color the map's border, places or roads pink.
Don't put a band behind a tool's title: the band is the error page's alone.
